clues: A capital stands on a winding river in the heart of a vast flat plain, where mixed forest fades into farmland, far from any sea.
Winter can plunge past minus thirty and drag on for months; summer answers with a short blast of heat past thirty-five — a sixty-five-degree swing.
A wooden hill fort grew into a princes' seat, survived a great invasion from the east, and became the heart of an empire touching two oceans.
Its fortress square holds a cathedral of candy-colored onion domes, and its subway stations look like underground palaces.
St. Basil's candy-striped domes rise over the great square at the city's very center.
